speaker: Doctor
text:
Good morning. I see you're experiencing postpartum fever and abdominal tenderness; to narrow this down, have you noticed any foul-smelling vaginal discharge or visible uterine deviations? Did you experience any shaking chills or severe pain during your most recent labor and delivery?

REQUEST TEST: Complete blood count (CBC), Urinalysis, and Endometrial Culture.

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum Endometritis.

Given your fever, uterine tenderness, foul-smelling discharge history, and recent delivery, this is the most likely diagnosis. The decreased bowel sounds may be secondary to pain or a concurrent urinary issue like a UTI, but the primary concern is an infection of the uterine lining.
